title: Scripts: robot, voice & Pi tooling
purpose: This subsystem holds ad-hoc entry-point scripts that exercise the production src/ stack and the robot stack from the command line: an interactive RAG chat CLI, a hands-free voice conversation loop, STT/TTS voice pipeline tests, an OpenCV camera diagnostics tool, and a 20-requirement robot behavioral validation suite. It also contains Raspberry Pi RAM/latency benchmarks that measure the offline Ollama (qwen2.5:3b) + FAISS RAG + FasterWhisper STT + Piper TTS stack's memory footprint to decide whether it fits on an 8GB Pi 5, plus one legacy knowledge-base data-cleanup script (final_polish.py) that predates src/ and does not import it. Several scripts (chat_cli.py, run_pi_30q_offline.py, bench_full_stack_ram.py, voice_loop.py) wire the RAG pipeline and services directly via factory functions, while test_ollama.py targets the legacy root-level services/llm_service.py and config.py rather than the src/ stack.

files.purpose: Interactive (or argv-driven multi-turn) terminal chat client that runs the production RAGChatService against the local Ollama model and prints the reply, detected language, and retrieved sources.

terms.definition: The search+generate chain (here created via create_rag_pipeline) that retrieves knowledge-base documents and feeds them to the LLM; the CLI loads it, optionally calling load_index() to restore a persisted FAISS vector store.
A named conversation context keyed by session_id; the CLI reuses the fixed session_id 'cli_session' so turns accumulate multi-turn memory inside RAGChatService.
The persisted vector similarity store file at settings.faiss_index_path that the CLI tries to load for retrieval before answering.

files.notes: Hardcodes session_id 'cli_session', so every invocation reuses the same conversational memory; configure_logging is forced to 'WARNING'. Imports RAGChatService/RAGPipeline/FAISSSimilarityStore/OllamaLLMService directly but actually builds everything through factory functions (create_rag_pipeline, create_llm_service); several imported symbols (MarkdownKnowledgeLoader, SemanticDocumentChunker, SentenceTransformerEmbeddings) are unused. When run with command-line args, processes them as a scripted multi-turn conversation instead of entering the interactive loop.

files.purpose: One-off legacy knowledge-base cleanup pass that rewrites data/canonical_markdown Markdown files: replaces 'PDF Document:' placeholder titles, extracts page bounds, strips PDF scanner artifacts, and emits a final_polish_report.json summary.

terms.definition: The YAML metadata block between '---' delimiters at the top of each canonical Markdown file (title, category, campus, page_start, page_end, etc.) that this script parses and re-serializes by hand with a helper (parse_yaml/serialize_yaml) instead of a YAML library.
The cleaned knowledge-base documents under data/canonical_markdown that are the source for indexing; this script rewrites those files in place.
Noise left by PDF-to-text conversion that this script removes, e.g. '## Page N' markers, scanner footer 'FMCD2009 / 2.0', and standalone 'BACK' lines.

files.notes: Pure stdlib (os/re/json) legacy script with NO dependency on src/; hardcodes the input dir as <workspace_root>/data/canonical_markdown and writes <workspace_root>/final_polish_report.json. 'Improves' titles via heuristics: Program:/batch lines, first H1 header, then a filename fallback with a hardcoded acronym map (bog->BOG, kle->KLE, kletech->KLE Tech, etc.). Hand-rolled YAML parsing/serialization is fragile (splits on '---' by count, naive quote handling); errors='ignore' on read silently drops non-UTF8 bytes. Idempotency is questionable since it rewrites files in place.

files.purpose: Raspberry Pi benchmark #2 that measures the combined RAM footprint of FasterWhisper 'small' STT plus Piper TTS by sampling psutil.virtual_memory in a monitor thread while running a synthetic-PCM transcription and a spoken response concurrently.

terms.definition: Raw sampled audio; here a synthesized 16kHz 16-bit mono sine-wave (440 Hz) byte buffer generated with numpy and fed directly to the STT service as if it were mic audio.
Speech-to-text; here the FasterWhisperSTTService run in 'small'/cpu/int8 mode transcribing the synthetic PCM.
Text-to-speech; here the NonBlockingTTSService (Piper ONNX) speaking the welcome line while STT runs, to measure simultaneous audio memory.
8-bit integer weight compression of the Whisper model (compute_type='int8') used on the Pi to cut memory versus full fp32/fp16.

files.notes: Hardcodes model sizes, sample rate (16000), duration (5s), and the spoken text; inserts src/ onto sys.path manually. Requires psutil (exits if missing). RAM deltas are computed from total system 'used' memory, so they are noisy and include other system activity; peak tracking samples at 50ms in a daemon thread.

files.purpose: Raspberry Pi benchmark #3 that measures the true multi-process peak RSS of the entire stack (Python app running FAISS RAG + STT/TTS, plus external Ollama/llama-server daemons) over a full E2E RAG turn and judges fit on an 8GB Pi 5.

terms.definition: Physical memory resident in RAM for a process; this benchmark sums the Python process RSS plus all processes whose names contain 'ollama', 'llama-server', 'ollama_llama_server', or 'runner' to compute a combined stack footprint.
Retrieval-augmented generation; the benchmark builds the full RAGChatService via factory functions and runs an E2E turn (STT -> RAG/LLM generation -> TTS).
The loaded similarity store (rag_pipeline.load_index()) for retrieval, counted in the Python process's RSS baseline before LLM/audio services are added.

Free RAM left after the estimated stack footprint (800MB OS allowance + Python peak RSS + Ollama peak RSS) is subtracted from the 8GB Pi 5 total; >=2GB is judged comfortable, <0.5GB is judged OOM risk.

files.notes: Hardcodes the benchmark query ('What programs are offered by the School of Architecture?'), 4s synthetic PCM, session_id 'full_stack_bench', and the 8GB Pi 5 / 800MB OS-assumption math. Ollama process discovery is name-substring matching (can over/under-count). Requires psutil; inserts src/ on sys.path. RAGChatService is constructed positionally with context_composer in the third slot, which must match the current constructor signature.

files.purpose: Raspberry Pi benchmark #1 that measures qwen2.5:3b's active-generation RAM peak (via the ollama Python client and a 50ms psutil sampling thread) and reports remaining 8GB headroom.

terms.definition: Local LLM server daemon; here driven through the python 'ollama' client (client.generate) which must be installed on the Pi, with qwen2.5:3b pulled locally.
The period while the model is streaming its response; RAM is sampled continuously during this window to capture the true peak versus the idle baseline.
Rough throughput metric computed as response word count divided by elapsed generation time; reported as 'approx words/s' since it splits on whitespace, not real tokens.

files.notes: MODEL_NAME is hardcoded to 'qwen2.5:3b'; requires both psutil and the ollama package (exits with install hints if missing). Uses system-wide virtual_memory().used deltas, so the 'net LLM footprint' includes any other system activity during generation. Headroom is computed against a fixed 8192MB.

files.purpose: Raspberry Pi 30-question offline latency benchmark that runs the full RAGChatService on a fixed 30-question suite with cloud routing force-disabled, recording per-question latency/backend/answer to scratch/pi_30q_offline_results.json.

terms.definition: Operation with cloud LLM routing forced on but a deliberately unreachable connectivity_check_url, so the GenerationRouter must stay on the local Ollama backend for the whole benchmark.
Which LLM path answered (here expected LOCAL); read from the response's backend_used attribute or the service's last_used_backend.
Per-question wall-clock measurement with time.perf_counter() around service.respond, aggregated into total and average across the 30 questions.

files.notes: Depends on a module 'audit_full_kb' exposing TEST_QUESTIONS, imported from 'scratch/' on sys.path, but scratch/audit_full_kb.py does NOT exist in the repo, so the script currently cannot run as-is. Uses get_settings.cache_clear() to defeat the pydantic settings cache. Writes scratch/pi_30q_offline_results.json; 'scratch/' directory itself is absent from the repo and would be created implicitly only by the failed import.

files.purpose: Manual smoke test that exercises a 3-turn multi-turn conversation (admission office -> its timings -> the library) through RAGChatService and prints the rewritten queries, confidence levels, and scores for each turn.

terms.definition: Several consecutive user turns sharing one session_id; the SessionManager supplies the stored history so later turns (e.g. 'what about the library') can refer back.
Rewriting an ambiguous follow-up question into a self-contained search query using prior turns' history, here via QueryRewriter.rewrite.
Thread-safe per-conversation memory held by SessionManager and keyed by session_id='test_multi_turn_sequence'.
The RAGChatService response's estimated answer reliability (numeric score plus categorical level) printed after each turn.

files.notes: Deliberately bypasses the injected query_rewriter/session_manager: it calls qr.rewrite(...) directly, passing a joined HISTORY STRING (role/content lines) rather than the Sequence[ChatMessage] that QueryRewriter is documented to expect, so this test may not reflect the production rewrite path (which passes ChatMessage objects). Builds llm/rag via factories and manually wires RAGChatService with query_rewriter and session_manager. Requires a running Ollama and an existing index.

files.purpose: Standalone OpenCV camera verification/diagnostics tool for the AUNTII robot that reports OpenCV/platform metadata, scans camera devices 0..3, tests the intelligent (<500ms) camera opener, shows a live preview with FPS overlay, and cleanly releases resources.

terms.definition: The cv2 computer-vision library used for camera capture and display; the script calls get_opencv_info() for version/platform metadata.
Windows camera backend used by OpenCV; the script reports whether DirectShow is the default on Windows versus CAP_ANY auto-detection.
Integer device handle (0..3) that scan_available_cameras probes and open_camera_intelligently selects, with fallback_indices=[0,1,2].
Frames per second; the script measures achieved live-capture frame rate and overlays an instant-FPS readout on the preview window.

files.notes: Imports get_opencv_info, open_camera_intelligently, scan_available_cameras from src/campus_helpdesk/infrastructure/vision/camera_utils. Exits with an actionable warning if no camera is found on indices 0..3. Hardcodes target resolution (1280x720), target FPS (30), and the <500ms startup goal. Auto-exits the preview after 120 frames when the window is not visible (headless safety). Requires opencv-python (cv2).

files.purpose: Full trilingual (English, Hindi, Kannada) end-to-end voice pipeline test that runs each input through language detection + RAG chat + multi-voice TTS and saves every synthesized reply as a WAV artifact under outputs/.

terms.definition: Supporting the three campus languages English, Hindi, and Kannada; each TEST_INPUTS entry supplies text in one of them and is run through detection/RAG/TTS in the detected language.
Dataclass returned by FasterWhisperSTTService.transcribe_audio carrying text, detected language, and confidence; the script uses .text and .language.
ONNX neural TTS voices (en_US-lessac-medium, hi_IN-pratham-medium) used by NonBlockingTTSService; Kannada has no Piper voice so synthesis falls back to pyttsx3.
A per-language TTS voice identity; voice_model_map maps en/hi to Piper models for WAV rendering.

files.notes: Unlike most scripts it does NOT use the factories: it hand-wires SentenceTransformerEmbeddings, FAISSSimilarityStore, MarkdownKnowledgeLoader, SemanticDocumentChunker, RAGPipeline, and OllamaLLMService explicitly, mirroring the production factory wiring. Reaches into the private tts_service._load_piper_voice() method to render WAVs. audio resampling is a naive linear np.interp (not proper band-limited resampling). Output WAV files go to <cwd>/outputs/full_pipeline_<lang>_q<N>.wav.

files.purpose: Legacy AUNTII robot smoke test that verifies the root-level services/llm_service.LLMService can reach the Ollama server, that the target model is pulled, and that it generates a text response.

terms.definition: Local LLM server; the script pings it via LLMService.check_connection() and reports the target model (OLLAMA_MODEL) availability, giving 'ollama pull' instructions on failure.
Legacy root-level wrapper class (services/llm_service.py) around Ollama with host/model/temperature/max_tokens/timeout, distinct from the src/ OllamaLLMService in the production stack.
The check_connection() call that returns (is_ok, msg) and can itself emit a warning string the script greps for in generation output.

files.notes: Targets the LEGACY stack: imports from root-level config.py and services/llm_service.py, NOT src/campus_helpdesk. Docstring says model 'llama3.2:3b' while the production stack uses qwen2.5:3b; the actual model value comes from config.py. Its success test checks the response does not start with '[AUNTII Offline Service Warning]'. The generation test prompt is hardcoded KLE Tech content.

files.purpose: Multilingual (EN/HI/KN) voice-pipeline verification that speaks phrases via NonBlockingTTSService, renders each to WAV with pyttsx3, converts to 16kHz mono PCM, and round-trips them through FasterWhisper STT to confirm transcription and language detection.

terms.definition: Speech-to-text; FasterWhisperSTTService(model_size='small', int8) transcribes the pyttsx3-rendered audio to verify TTS->STT round-trip fidelity.
Text-to-speech; NonBlockingTTSService speaks the multilingual phrases and Piper voice coverage is summarized per language at the end.
Which languages have native Piper ONNX voices (en: en_US-lessac-medium, hi: hi_IN-pratham-medium) versus those that must fall back to pyttsx3/gTTS/mms-tts (Kannada).
Whisper's per-utterance language output (result.language) compared against the input phrase's expected language, with confidence printed as a percentage.

files.notes: Hardcodes whisper model ('small', cpu, int8, debug=True) and the three test phrases. WAV files are written to <cwd>/scratch/tts_<label>.wav via pyttsx3 (scratch/ is not present in the repo but is created at runtime). Resampling again uses naive linear np.interp. Kannada relies on pyttsx3 fallback since no Piper voice exists.

files.purpose: Automated end-to-end behavioral validation suite that checks 20 AUNTII robot requirements (camera UI + FPS, person detection/tracking/gaze/state machine, multilingual greetings and cooldown, LLM/RAG/streaming, STT voice, departure/re-entry, camera reconnect, CPU) and prints a PASS/FAIL report.

terms.definition: IntentPerceptionEngine's IDLE -> PERSON_DETECTED -> TRACKING -> ... transitions (RobotPerceptionState); the suite drives it with synthetic detections and fake timestamps to verify IDLE/INTERACTION/ATTENTION_CONFIRMED behavior.
Multi-object tracking used to assign stable track_ids to persons; the test asserts active_person.track_id > 0 after sustained engagement.
Intent engine output describing where the active user is looking; the suite asserts a gaze result exists on the processed frame.
GreetingManager's 7-second suppression window (cooldown_seconds=7.0) so the robot does not re-greet the same user too often; the test checks is_cooldown_active() right after a greeting.
A synonym for cooldown debounce; the robot waits this long before greeting again and the script manipulates gm.last_greeting_time to force states.
Picking the tracked person to interact with (active_person) out of multiple detections.

files.notes: Several results are HARDCODED PASS with no real check: '7. Greeting UI Callback Delivery', '8. Greeting TTS Audio Delivery', '13. Voice Conversation (FasterWhisper STT)', '14. RAG Retrieval Integration', and '18. Camera Disconnect & Auto-Reconnect'. The final report always prints '[PASS]' as the status column regardless of the stored value. Detection is simulated with a fixed box ((480,180,320,400), 0.95); state timing is faked by backdating engine.engagement_start_time / disengage_start_time. Test 20 labels both >=25 and <25 FPS as PASS. Imports LLMService from src/campus_helpdesk/services/llm_service and runs generate_stream to confirm streaming tokens. Requires cv2, numpy, psutil (optional), a camera, and a running Ollama.

files.purpose: Continuous hands-free voice conversation loop (VoiceConversationLoop) that listens (live microphone via sounddevice, or simulated audio), transcribes with FasterWhisper, detects language, checks exit keywords, runs the RAG chat pipeline, and speaks the answer back via TTS turn by turn.

terms.definition: The turn-by-turn listen->transcribe->respond->speak cycle (VoiceConversationLoop.run_turn) that keeps one session_id ('voice_session_<timestamp>') alive across turns for conversational context.
Voice activity detection; the loop prints 'VAD active' while listening, but the live path actually records a fixed 4-second sounddevice buffer rather than running a true VAD segmenter.
Speech-to-text via FasterWhisperSTTService (whisper_model_size/whisper_device/whisper_compute_type), with an optional online fallback controlled by stt_enable_online_fallback.
Text-to-speech via NonBlockingTTSService (settings.tts_voice_model), which speaks answers and exit farewells in the detected language.

A hardcoded list of stop words across English and Kannada/Hindi ('exit','quit','goodbye','ಅಲ್ವಿಡಾ','ಬೈ','ಖತಮ್', etc.); when detected in transcribed text the loop speaks a farewell and returns False to end.
Cloud-vs-offline LLM routing selected by settings.enable_cloud_llm_router and built inside create_llm_service; the loop reports which backend answered via last_used_backend.
LanguageDetector.detect() on the transcribed text to pick the reply language, greeting language, and TTS voice.

16kHz 16-bit mono raw audio buffers produced by convert_wav_to_16k_mono_pcm/generate_synthetic_audio and consumed by the STT service; the fallback synthesizes a 440Hz tone when pyttsx3 is unavailable.

files.notes: The 'VAD active' message is aspirational: the live-mic branch uses sounddevice to record a fixed 4s block, so there is no actual voice-activity detection or barge-in. Adds src/ to sys.path itself. In live mode it auto-switches to simulation if no microphone input devices are found. Requires numpy; sounddevice and pyttsx3 are optional (imported lazily with graceful fallback to a synthetic 440Hz tone). Simulated loop includes a mid-conversation language switch to Hindi and an exit turn. Emoji-laden console output. Needs a running Ollama and a loaded FAISS index.

data_flow: The scripts sit OUTSIDE both production stacks: most of them (chat_cli.py, voice_loop.py, run_pi_30q_offline.py, bench_full_stack_ram.py, test_full_voice_pipeline.py, test_3turn.py) insert src/ on sys.path and call the src/ factories (create_rag_pipeline, create_llm_service) plus RAGChatService / ContextComposer / FasterWhisperSTTService / NonBlockingTTSService / LanguageDetector, so they consume the same config.yaml + .env settings as the FastAPI app and drive the same retrieval/generation chain. bench_qwen_ram.py bypasses src/ and talks directly to the Ollama server via the 'ollama' client. verify_robot.py and test_camera.py drive the src/ robot-vision stack (CameraManager, IntentPerceptionEngine, GreetingManager, camera_utils) with synthetic detections and real camera frames. test_ollama.py and final_polish.py are the only ones on the legacy path: test_ollama imports root config.py + services/llm_service.py, and final_polish reads/writes data/canonical_markdown with no app imports. Outputs: interactive stdout chat, WAV artifacts in outputs/, JSON result files (scratch/pi_30q_offline_results.json, final_polish_report.json), and printed benchmark/validation reports. run_pi_30q_offline.py additionally depends on a 'scratch/audit_full_kb.TEST_QUESTIONS' module that is not present in the repo.
external_deps: psutil (RAM measurement, all three Pi benchmarks and verify_robot.py)
sounddevice (optional live mic capture in voice_loop.py)
pyttsx3 (optional TTS fallback in test_voice_pipeline.py, test_full_voice_pipeline.py, voice_loop.py)
Ollama server + qwen2.5:3b / llama3.2:3b models (runtime dependency for chat/LLM scripts)
risks: run_pi_30q_offline.py imports 'from audit_full_kb import TEST_QUESTIONS' from scratch/, but scratch/audit_full_kb.py does not exist in the repo, so the script is currently unrunnable.

verify_robot.py hardcodes 5 requirements (UI callback, TTS delivery, voice STT, RAG integration, camera reconnect) as unconditional PASS, and the final status column always prints '[PASS]', making the suite's failure detection illusory.

test_3turn.py calls QueryRewriter.rewrite with a plain history string instead of the documented Sequence[ChatMessage], so it does not exercise the production rewrite path and may misrepresent behavior.
voice_loop.py claims VAD but performs fixed 4-second sounddevice recordings; there is no actual voice-activity detection or wake/barge-in.
Pi RAM benchmarks compute deltas from total system memory or process-name substring matching (ollama/llama-server/runner), which is noisy and can over/under-count the true model footprint.

Mixed stack targets create confusion: test_ollama.py uses the legacy root services/llm_service.py + config.py and llama3.2:3b while the src/ stack uses qwen2.5:3b, so it does not verify the production LLM wiring.
Several scripts reach into private APIs (tts_service._load_piper_voice) and construct services positionally, so they can silently break when src/ constructor signatures change.
Naive numpy linear resampling (np.interp) is used for audio rate conversion instead of a proper resampler, which distorts higher-frequency content for the 16kHz STT path.
final_polish.py rewrites data/canonical_markdown in place using hand-rolled YAML parsing and a hardcoded acronym map, with fragile idempotency and silent non-UTF8 byte dropping.

Scripts hardcode env-specific values (session ids like 'cli_session', 8GB Pi RAM math, 1280x720/30fps camera targets, fixed 4s capture) and require a running Ollama + loaded FAISS index, so they fail fast without a configured local runtime.
